N vs N. Sreenivasa Naidu on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165370902/
1  **

* *
 ::JUDGMENT:

: 
This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
2.

The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 17.01.2022 at about 8.15 a.m. he had been waiting for a bus at Jodi HosaHalli Village Gate, on ChintamaniBengaluru Road, Chintamani Taluk,
Chikkaballapura Disrict, a bus bearing Reg.No.KA40 SCCH5 6800 came in high speed rash and negligently and dashed against him, due to the said accident, he has sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, he was taken to Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic & Surgical Hospital Kolar,
wherein he has taken treatment as indoor patient and spent an amount of Rs.3,00,000/ towards treatment, medicines, conveyance.
3. At the time of the accident he was aged about 27 years, hale and healthy, working as mason,
thereby earning Rs.20,000/ p.m., due to this accident he has lost his income and earning capacity.
Out of this accident crime No.25/2022 is registered against the driver of the said bus before the Chintamani Rural Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
R1 is the owner, R2 is insurer of the said bus, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to SCCH5 allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.25,00,000/.
4.

On service of notice, R1/owner has appeared and filed written statement denying case of the petitioner by stating that, petition filed by the petitioner is not legally maintainable, further submitted that, he is R.C.Owner of the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA406800 and said vehicle is duly insured with R2 vide its policy No.110522123400006538 valid since 17.11.2021 to 16.11.2022 and if there is any liability to pay the compensation, R2 is liable to pay the same.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5. R2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement denying entire case of the petitioner, further a d m i t s i s s u a n c e o f p o l i c y t o b u s b e a r i n g R e g . N o .
K A 4 0  6 8 0 0 v i d e p o l i c y No.110522123400006538 valid since SCCH5 17.11.2021 to 16.11.2022, claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
6. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following:

::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 17.01.2022 at about 8.15 a.m. when petitioner was waiting for a Bus at Jodi Hosahalli Village Gate on ChintamaniBengaluru Road,
Chintamani Taluk, Chikkaballapura District, at that time, Bus bearing Reg.No.KA 406800 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the Venkatesha.N vs N. Sreenivasa Naidu on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165370902/
2 petitioner, as mentioned in claim petition?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so how much and from whom?
SCCH5 3. What order or award?
7. In order to prove his case, petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW1, examined 2 witnesses as PW2 and PW3 and marked 15 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.15 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, counsel for R2 submitted that, he has no defence evidence.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1: In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW1, in his chief SCCH5 examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of wound certificate is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.6.
10.

The counsel for R1 and R2 have cross examined the PW1 stating that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the petitioner and there is no negligency of the bus driver, but such suggestions is denied by the petitioner.
Further there is no dispute about place, date and time of the accident.

Police papers marked at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.6 speaks that, very accident is occurred on 17.01.2022 at about 8.15 a.m. at SCCH5 Jodihosahalli Village Gate on Chintamani - Bengaluru road while waiting for the bus, further this accident is caused by the negligency of the driver of the bus bearing Reg.No.KA406800.
Further there is no dispute about place, date and time of the accident.
On the other hand, there is no defence evidence.
Considering the same, believing the version of the petitioner, I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:
As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained left femoral medial condyle fracture with head of fibula with impending compartment syndrome left leg with foot drop.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.5, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.7 issued by Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic & Surgical Hospital wherein he took SCCH5 treatment as Venkatesha.N vs N. Sreenivasa Naidu on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165370902/
3 indoor patient since 17.01.2022 to 21.01.2022.

Xray Films are marked as Ex.P.11.
12.
Further Dr.Nagaraj B.N. Orthopaedic Surgeon at SOADS is examined as PW2 and furnished clinical notes marked as Ex.P.12, Xray Films marked as Ex.P.13.

He has assessed physical disability of the lower limb at the rate of 49% and whole body disability at the rate of 16%.
13.

In crossexamination admits that, fractures are united, implants in situ, he has not seen the follow up records, fracture was at the knee joint, restrictions is also only on knee joint, there is no superficial complication to the petitioner, he has not treated the petitioner.
wound certificate marked at Ex.P.5 speaks that, there are two fractures on left leg.

Further Ex.P.7 discharge summary speaks about taking of treatment in SCCH5 Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic & Surgical Hospital as indoor patient since 17.01.2022 to 21.01.2022, OR+IF with cc screws for medial condyle femur is made on 18.01.2022, accordingly there is medical bill for an amount of Rs.1,07,428/.

14. Petitioner is a mason, aged about 27 years, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the bus driver, non treated Doctor Nagaraj has assessed the disability of particular limb at the rate of 49%
and whole body disability at the rate of 16%, but looking to the nature of the injuries, treatment taken by him, age and nature of work, whole body disability is considered at the rate of 10%, which will be taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.
15.
Further record section clerk at Gaurav Hospital Kolar is examined as PW3 and furnished SCCH5 authorization letter marked as Ex.P.14, case sheet marked as Ex.P.15.
In cross examination admits that, he do not know the contents of the documents produced by him.

16. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 27 years, for proof of his age, copy of aadhar card is on record, wherein it is clearly mentioned year of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 1994, the alleged accident is occurred on 2022, considering the same his age is considered about 28 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 17 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

entities.text: Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. As per his case, he was working as mason, thereby earning Rs.20,000/ p.m., to prove the said fact, SCCH5 there are no documents on record.
Hence considering the same, this court relied upon the Karnataka Minimum Wages for the year 202223.

In the case on hand, petitioner is mason,
nature of work is not mentioned in the petition, so that, he comes under the category of formerly groupIV - now unskilled worker category.

Very accident is occurred on 17.01.2022, accordingly as on the date of accident including dearness allowances for unskilled workers minimum wages for a month will come to Rs.13,821/, so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

Therefore, the loss of future income works out as under;
13,821/x12x17x10% = Rs.2,81,948/.
Venkatesha.N vs N. Sreenivasa Naidu on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165370902/
4 SCCH5 18.

Keeping in mind injuries caused to the petitioner, treatment taken, expenses incurred and also the pain suffered, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, it is just and necessary to allot compensation under other heads, accordingly for pain and sufferings compensation of Rs.15,000/
is awarded, for conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges Rs.15,000/ is awarded, for loss of amenities of life Rs.15,000/ is awarded
, further he is entitled for Rs.13,821/ towards loss of income during laid up period.

Further petitioner is also entitled for compensation for medical expenses incurred by him, for which, he has produced medical bills marked as Ex.P.9 for an amount of Rs.1,07,428/ stating that he has spent the said amount for treatment.

On the other hand, there is crossexamination stating that, there is no such expenses and there is no advance SCCH5 bill, but mere denial there is no any cogent evidence by the respondents to disprove the case of the petitioners with regard to the medical bills.
Hence this court comes to the conclusion that, medical bills of Rs.1,07,428/ furnished by the petitioner is borne by him and which is proper and correct.
19. Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:
Sl. No.

Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of future income 2,81,94800 2. Pain and sufferings 15,00000 3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,00000 attendant charges 4.
Medical Expenses 1,07,42800 5.
Loss of amenities in life 15,00000 6.
Loss of income during laid up 13,82100 period Total 4,48,19700 SCCH5 20.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,48,197/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

21. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.110522123400006538, which is valid for the period from 17.11.2021 to 16.11.2022, the alleged accident was occurred on 17.01.2022, it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.
Further there is no dispute about non holding of driving license by the driver of the offending bus.
So that, R2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
SCCH5 22. Issue No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
Venkatesha.N vs N. Sreenivasa Naidu on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165370902/
5 ::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,48,197/ (Rupees Four Lakhs Forty Eight Thousand One Hundred Ninety Seven Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through epayment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
SCCH5 The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.

(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, typed by her, thereof is corrected and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 12th day of January, 2024)
(MALAKARI RAMAPPA WADEYAR) VIII ADDL. JUDGE & ACMM, MEMBER,
MACT, BENGALURU.
